materials.title: At the music room
materials.text:
Choose the best reply in each conversation.

1. Teacher: Is this your first piano lesson?
Child: ____

2. Child: Where should I put my bag?
Teacher: ____

3. Teacher: Please listen before you try.
Child: ____

4. Teacher: Was that note high or low?
Child: ____

5. Child: May I try the short tune again?
Teacher: ____

questions.prompt:
Teacher: Is this your first piano lesson?
Child: ____
options: Yes. I have not played before.
questions.explanation: Yes confirms first lesson and lack of previous playing. Place/count/coat colour do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: Where should I put my bag?
Teacher: ____
questions.explanation: Under the chair supplies a bag location. Preference/day/family do not.

questions.prompt:
Teacher: Please listen before you try.
Child: ____
options: All right. I will wait and listen.
questions.explanation: Waiting/listening follows the instruction. Age/vehicle/pet do not.

questions.prompt:
Teacher: Was that note high or low?
Child: ____
questions.explanation: Low chooses one pitch category. Time/count/place do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: May I try the short tune again?
Teacher: ____
options: Of course. Start when you are ready.
questions.explanation: Permission to start answers may I. Colour/home/family do not.

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: A missing mitten identifies the loss. Weather/place/person do not.

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

units.title: The tail on the blue kite
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The tail on the blue kite
materials.text: Ben has a blue kite. On Saturday, he takes it to the park with Dad. The kite has a long yellow tail. Ben runs across the grass, and the kite goes up. Then the tail catches on a low branch. Dad helps him bring the kite down without pulling hard. The yellow paper has a small hole. At home, Ben puts a patch over it. He uses red paper because there is no yellow paper left. On Sunday, the kite flies again. Its tail now has one red spot. Ben likes being able to recognise his kite in the sky.

questions.prompt: Ben’s kite is blue.
questions.explanation: The first sentence states blue.

questions.prompt: The whole tail is red at first.
questions.explanation: The original tail is yellow; only the repair adds a red spot.

questions.prompt: The tail catches on a branch.
questions.explanation: A low branch catches the tail.

questions.prompt: Ben uses yellow paper for the patch.
questions.explanation: No yellow remains, so red is used.

questions.prompt: Ben flies the kite again on Sunday.
questions.explanation: Sunday flight is explicitly stated.

units.title: The cucumber in the shopping bag
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The cucumber in the shopping bag
materials.text: Mum asks Anna to help unpack the shopping. Anna puts apples in the fruit bowl and bread in the bread box. A long green cucumber is at the bottom of the bag. Anna thinks it is a strange banana and puts it with the apples. Mum smiles and shows her the label. They wash the cucumber and cut some for lunch. Anna likes the cool slices in her sandwich. She draws the cucumber on a small card and writes its name. The card goes on the fridge. Next time, Anna says, the cucumber will not have to visit the fruit bowl first.

questions.prompt: Anna helps unpack shopping.
questions.explanation: Mum asks her to help unpack.

questions.prompt: The bread goes in the fruit bowl.
questions.explanation: Apples go there; bread goes in bread box.

questions.prompt: Anna first puts the cucumber with the apples.
questions.explanation: She mistakes it for a banana and puts it with apples.

questions.prompt: They use some cucumber for lunch.
questions.explanation: They wash and cut some for lunch sandwiches.

questions.prompt: The drawing goes inside Anna’s shoe.
questions.explanation: The card goes on the fridge.

units.title: A chair for the teddy bear
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: A chair for the teddy bear
materials.text: Leo makes a chair for his teddy bear from a small cardboard box. He cuts a back and two arms, then covers the seat with cloth. The chair looks good, but it falls over when Teddy sits down. Leo tries again with a wider piece of card under the box. This time, the chair stays up. His sister paints little flowers on the back. Leo does not paint the seat because the cloth is already soft and blue. At bedtime, Teddy sits in the chair beside Leo’s bed. Leo checks once more that it is steady before he turns off the light.

questions.prompt: Leo makes the chair from cardboard.
questions.explanation: The main box and supporting card are cardboard.

questions.prompt: The chair stays up on the first try.
questions.explanation: It initially falls when Teddy sits.

questions.prompt: A wider piece of card helps it stand.
questions.explanation: The added base steadies it.

questions.prompt: Leo’s sister paints flowers on the seat.
questions.explanation: She paints back; seat stays blue cloth.

questions.prompt: The chair is beside Leo’s bed at night.
questions.explanation: Bedtime placement is beside bed.

units.title: The tall flower by the gate
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The tall flower by the gate
materials.text: There is a tall sunflower beside our garden gate. My little sister calls it the garden sun. In the morning, she counts its big green leaves with me. We count eight, but one small leaf is hidden behind the stem. Mum shows it to us, and we change our number to nine. My sister wants to pick the flower for her room. Mum asks her to leave it for everyone to see. We draw a picture instead. My sister puts the picture above her desk. The real flower stays by the gate, where the post worker smiles at it every morning.

questions.prompt: The sunflower grows beside the gate.
questions.explanation: Its location is garden gate.

questions.prompt: The children first count nine leaves.
questions.explanation: They first count eight, then discover ninth.

questions.prompt: One small leaf is hidden behind the stem.
questions.explanation: Mum points out that hidden leaf.

questions.prompt: They pick the flower for the bedroom.
questions.explanation: They draw it instead and leave flower growing.

questions.prompt: The picture goes above the sister’s desk.
questions.explanation: That is stated picture location.

units.title: A card for the bus driver
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: A card for the bus driver
materials.text: Our school bus driver is Mr Green. On Friday, our class makes him a thank-you card. We draw a yellow bus on the front. Inside, every child writes a name. I write mine in blue, but my friend Sam uses green. We give the card to Mr Green after he parks the bus at school. He does not open it while driving. At lunchtime, our teacher shows us a photograph. Mr Green is holding the card and smiling. He has put it on the little table in the staff room. Sam says a green name was a good choice for Mr Green.

questions.prompt: The class makes a card on Friday.
questions.explanation: Friday is stated.

questions.prompt: The bus on the card is purple.
questions.explanation: The drawn bus is yellow.

questions.prompt: Sam writes his name in green.
questions.explanation: Narrator blue, Sam green.

questions.prompt: Mr Green opens the card while driving.
questions.explanation: He explicitly does not; card given after parking.

questions.prompt: The card is on a table in the staff room.
questions.explanation: Photo shows its staff-room table location.
